# fuzz fixture: one run per seed, one line per random legal action.
# The fixture is generated by tools/gen_fuzz_fixture.py; do not edit.
# Every blind's target is forced to 1 chip at the top of each step, before
# the record, so both engines see target 1 and any play beats the blind.
# The action is chosen uniformly from legal_actions() by a seeded
# random.Random on the Python side and applied verbatim by Rust, so the
# chooser never has to be mirrored.
# Columns: phase ante action money hands discards hand jokers consumables
#          shop pack chips rng selection digests legal
#
# `action` is structured (type=..;index=..;cards=..), not repr.
# `selection` is the picking handed to state_dict: the action's own card
# indices for a PLAY or DISCARD (what the agent would hold) and empty for
# every other step. This is a reconstruction, not the real environment's
# picking; it is emitted so both engines are handed the identical one.
#
# `digests` is one `key=<16 hex>` pair per top-level state_dict key (42),
# `;`-joined and sorted by key; each is FNV-1a-64 over that key's
# `path<TAB>value` leaves joined by newlines (tools/state_render.py).
#
# `legal` is the point of this fixture:
#     legal_order=<hex>   legal actions in legal_actions() order
#     legal_sorted=<hex>  the same list sorted by the action's rendering
# Each hashes the canonical leaves of `[<action repr>, ...]`. A mismatch
# only in `_order` is a wrong ORDER; a mismatch in `_sorted` (and so
# usually both) is a MISSING OR EXTRA action. `--dump <SEED> <STEP>`
# prints the list in canonical order with the chosen one marked.
